Hello Link

Your question is very important, and being discussed alot all over.

Yes, different server time is effecting H4 and Daily bars. there also some issues with the begining of the week, aka: sunday bars. This is mainly effecting trading indicators such as Moving averages, and pivots calculations. LUCKY FOR US - WE DON'T NEED ANY INDICATORS.

About the H4, you just need to know there ire differences of the charts patterns - But with S&D discipline we see the big picture, that is Low Time Frames and High and consider all at once. So the H4 will never be the only cause for taking a trade.

About Daily bars. it's only effects the open and the close of the day, and might add a little awkward sunday bar. so you will have to be aware of that. Most brokers with GMT 0 and up will not have the sunday bar. and for the open close time, consider it as you would with your H4.

Hi Romant,

An engulf is an indicator that power is changing hands in this particular zone, it needs to be accompanied by a nice un tapped supply or demand zone so that you are starting to stack the odds in favor of your trade.

Hi HRT,

If you are new to Supply and Demand than I suggest to just try to trade the fresh zones. Just make sure that you know what the leading directions are from Higher Time Frames zones.

Start your weekly analysis by looking at where price is on the HTF's. For example What is the direction price is trading at the moment on Monthly, Weekly, Daily, 4h. Are we trading towards Supply or Demand? Did we just left Supply or Demand?

Once you become comfortable at trading only fresh zones, you than can start looking at tested zones.

I encourage you to get some screen time too. Draw your zones of intrest and watch how price reacts to it. This is a great way to learn more.

Once you have your zones in place, look at the approach, is price compressing up towards your fresh supply/demand than it's a good thing. Let price show you what it wants to do and then trade in synch with it.

Also, you really want to look at the potential target. If you have a fresh supply zone and there is not a lot of room for price to move, than as a beginner you can skip the opportunity and look for a beter place to trade elswhere.

If you are new, I suggest you don't risk real money while learning. You can learn on a demo accout but yet treat it like it was real money. This is where you will get your discipline from. If you are really serious and dedicated about your future trading career, you got to be disciplined and put a lot of time and dedication to have this working. The good news for you is that you already found out that supply and demand is an important part of trading, this gives you an edge over other traders but like I said earlier there is a lot more to look at than just pure s/d but you'll discover all this set by step.

So try to digest all the above and than make a decision. Are you willing to put the time and effort that is needed to become succesfull or are you not.

Wishing you all the best anyway. Mel
